A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same object-detection debiasing framework despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original controlled augmentation experiments, synthesis and detection evaluations on MS COCO and NuImages, and component ablations in Sections 2 and 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds detector generalization experiments, further ablations, a three-run stability analysis and class-distribution results.

M1.justification: The RS calculation and update, layout recalibration, blueprint conditioning and generative-alignment objective remain unchanged in Equations 1–14. New quantization descriptions and renderer pseudocode document implementation details rather than establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS COCO and NuImages for layout-to-image fidelity and object-detection debiasing across location, category frequency and size. Additional detector architectures and component tests retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds GDCC to Table 1 at both synthesis resolutions; v1 cited this work but did not include these comparisons. New Table 10 also evaluates GeoDiffusion with scoring-driven debiasing. Existing debiasing comparator sets are retained, including v1 Table S2, now Table S4.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands beyond Faster R-CNN to YOLOX-s, DINO and CO-DETR in Table 9. V2 also introduces controlled generator/debiasing combinations and a five-setting β sweep. These substantially extend the tested configurations and controls; existing dataset splits, metrics, synthesis resolutions and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds blueprint-component fidelity ablations, separates visual and contextual diversity contributions in the expanded RS ablation, tests generator/debiasing dependence, and adds β sensitivity, alignment stability and class-distribution analyses. Existing ablations and qualitative examples are retained, so these are substantive additions rather than appendix relocations.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without repeated-run counts or dispersion. V2 Table S3 first reports mean mAP and standard deviation across three independently seeded training runs, with and without alignment. This reporting is limited to that study and does not establish repeated evaluation of all main results.

E6.justification: Existing main-method scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 9 newly reports augmentation gains of 2.8, 2.8 and 2.6 mAP for YOLOX-s, DINO and CO-DETR. Added GDCC results narrow the best-comparator COCO 512-resolution margin from 15.9 to 13.9 mAP and show better NuImages FID than the proposed method, 7.97 versus 8.35. New ablation and stability results appear. Figure S1 also changes reported gains, including spoon from +4.8% to +6.8% and cat from +4.4% to +3.2%, and removes horse.

T1.justification: The core mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–14 are retained, with notation and typesetting adjustments. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive derivation. Its new pseudocode elaborates implementation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: diagnosing representation gaps beyond frequency, RS-guided recalibration, visual blueprints and generative alignment. The headline gains of 4.4/3.6 mAP for large/rare instances and 15.9 mAP for synthesis layout accuracy are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations that separated HSV colors improve encoder discrimination and alignment prevents overfitting to stochastic synthetic artifacts. It interprets Table 10 as showing high-fidelity synthesis is prerequisite to effective targeted debiasing, and the new distribution plot as evidence of tail enrichment. These elaborate mechanisms without changing the central interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 discloses RS quantization, default β=1, blueprint construction pseudocode and approximately 74 GPU-hours for generator training. However, Section 3.1 describes an M×M positional grid and logarithmic size bins, whereas Appendix A.3 specifies ten horizontal bins and three COCO size categories. These conflicting disclosures do not establish an actual setting change. The repository URL is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for YOLOX, DINO, CO-DETR and several generation/augmentation works, while removing Gal et al. (2022) and Peebles and Xie (2023). It also makes the distinction from simple ControlNet class maps more explicit. The broader positioning against frequency-centric debiasing and textual layout conditioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, affiliations and conference header change. V2 locally expands method explanations, revises diagnostic discussion, adds appendix subsections and inserts acknowledgement, ethics and reproducibility statements. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained; several new cross-references are incorrect or unfinished.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overall pipeline diagram, a class-map comparison, a class-distribution plot, five result/analysis tables and a pseudocode display. It expands the RS table, revises Figure S1 and rearranges existing displays while retaining the six appendix qualitative grids. The new distribution plot duplicates the Figure S3 label used by a retained qualitative figure.

improvement.justification: The additional detector tests, targeted ablations and first uncertainty estimate strengthen support for the unchanged method, while the overview and pseudocode improve explanation. The net gain is limited by conflicting RS quantization descriptions, broken references and the retained 15.9 mAP headline despite the stronger GDCC comparator newly reported in Table 1.
